label: copy phase, mid-sequence (recall 2-4, long L), favoring outputs of d/i/h/s/u/v/x
explanation: Fires almost exclusively in the copy phase (100% of mass; never on original tokens, essentially never at <DEL>), concentrated at recall_idx 2-4 / t 10-12 in long sequences (L 7-9; silent for L<=4). Within that window it is strongly token-selective on the output: out_tok d has 12.9x lift and 32% of mass, with i, h, s, u, v, x next; the step before outputting d (next_out d) also lifts 7.8x. The strongest activations (up to 4.2) are on the copy step whose output is a d at original position 2-3, with weaker activations on the neighbouring steps (the one before and the d input itself). Not position-only (copy phase alone F1 0.11) and not d-only (out_tok==d recall 0.21); the best simple predicate reaches F1 ~0.37, mass recall ~0.49 on dev, so the selectivity is broad/distributed over many output tokens and the description is incomplete.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: d, i, h, s, v, u; least: e, j, z, g) and the next token to output (most: d, h, i, l, r, 2; least: -, j, z, e); timing cues that raise it most: L=9, t=17, recall_idx=8.
